narrative.overview: This is a researcher's field instrument, not a productivity app performing for engagement. Every screen reads as a page from a geological survey — precise, institutional, legible under dim field conditions. The palette draws from USGS topographic maps: a dark forest ground replaces the daylight paper of the original, but the color vocabulary is the same one Montana ranchers read daily.
keyCharacteristics: Single dark surface family (forest ground → survey panel → survey panel raised), dark-only
One accent color carries all primary/active/interactive meaning: survey blue
Flat by default — depth comes from tonal layering, not shadows
Section grid on the page ground (160px repeating linear gradient)
Station numbers on conversation list entries
No eyebrows or kickers above headings

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Survey Blue is the only color allowed to mean 'primary.'

rules.name: The Grid Ground Rule
rules.body: The section grid on the page background is the world's signature material.

rules.name: The Fluid-Only Rule
rules.body: Headings never get a fixed pixel size.

dos: Do keep Survey Blue as the only color meaning 'primary.'
Do convey elevation with tonal steps only, never shadows.
Do keep every screen single-column inside the 768px container.
Do pair Vegetation Green and Topo Red with an icon or text, never color alone.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color.
Don't add eyebrows or kickers above headings.
Don't add a sidebar, tab bar, or multi-column layout.
Don't use Amber Marker or Vegetation Green decoratively.
